reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement for both compounds. Avelumab trough concentrations reached 39.11 μg/mL by cycle 6, indicating adequate PD-L1 engagement. Axitinib at 5mg BID is within the established therapeutic range for VEGFR inhibition. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The combination demonstrated clear biological activity with PD-L1 positive tumor identification (266/434 vs 288/439) and the synergistic mechanism is supported by the superior efficacy in both PD-L1 positive and negative subgroups compared to sunitinib monotherapy. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint was met with PFS HR 0.61 (p=0.0001) in PD-L1 positive patients. Overall PFS was 13.8 vs 8.4 months compared to sunitinib, with ORR 51.4% vs 25.7%. OS showed positive trend but didn't reach significance (HR 0.86, p=0.1509). 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: The combination showed benefit across both PD-L1 positive (13.8 vs 7.2 months) and PD-L1 negative (16.1 vs 11.1 months) subgroups, suggesting broad population benefit. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Well-powered study (n=886) with appropriate duration (387 weeks). Higher toxicity in combination arm (136 vs 65 discontinuations) but did not prevent efficacy demonstration.

failure_modes.evidence: Higher discontinuation rate due to toxicity in combination arm (136 vs 65) and increased hepatotoxicity, but this did not prevent demonstration of efficacy
